faq.q1: How do I calculate a percentage of a number?
faq.a1: Multiply the number by the percentage and divide by 100. For example, 15% of 200 = 200 × 15 ÷ 100 = 30.
faq.q2: How do I find what percent one number is of another?
faq.a2: Divide the first number by the second and multiply by 100. For example, 30 ÷ 200 × 100 = 15%.
faq.q3: How do I calculate percentage increase or decrease?
faq.a3: Subtract the starting value from the final value, divide by the absolute value of the starting value, and multiply by 100. A positive result is an increase, a negative one is a decrease.
faq.q4: How do I add or subtract a percentage?
faq.a4: To add a percentage, multiply the number by (1 + percent / 100). To subtract, use (1 minus percent / 100). For example, 200 + 15% = 200 × 1.15 = 230.
faq.q5: How do I extract VAT from a total?
faq.a5: Divide the gross amount by (1 + rate / 100). For example, 120 at 20%: 120 ÷ 1.20 = 100 — that is the net amount.
faq.q6: Can I use decimals in this calculator?
faq.a6: Yes. All fields accept decimal values, and results are shown with up to four decimal places.

compound-interest-calculator.title: Compound Interest Calculator – Future Value of Investment
compound-interest-calculator.description: Free compound interest calculator. See how your money grows with different compounding frequencies and time horizons.
compound-interest-calculator.keywords: compound interest calculator,compound interest,future value calculator,investment growth

faq.a1: Compound interest is interest earned on both the initial principal and the accumulated interest from previous periods. Over time, this creates exponential growth.
faq.q2: What is the compound interest formula?
faq.a2: A = P × (1 + r/n)^(n×t), where P is the principal, r is the annual interest rate, n is the number of compounding periods per year, and t is the time in years.
faq.q3: What is the effective annual rate?
faq.a3: The effective annual rate (EAR) is the actual return over one year after accounting for compounding within the year. A higher compounding frequency means a higher EAR for the same nominal rate.
faq.q4: How does compounding frequency affect returns?
faq.a4: More frequent compounding means interest is added to the balance more often, so it starts earning interest sooner. Daily compounding yields the highest return, annual the lowest — for the same nominal rate.

discount-calculator.title: Discount Calculator – Final Price After Discount & Tax

faq.q1: How do I calculate a discount?
faq.a1: Multiply the original price by the discount percentage and divide by 100 to get the savings. Subtract savings from the original price to get the discounted price.
faq.q2: How do I add sales tax after a discount?
faq.a2: First calculate the discounted price (price minus savings), then multiply it by the tax rate and divide by 100. Add the tax amount to the discounted price for the final total.
faq.q3: Is tax applied before or after the discount?
faq.a3: In most jurisdictions, sales tax is applied after the discount. You pay tax only on the price you actually pay, not the original price.
faq.q4: Can I use this for multiple items?
faq.a4: This calculator handles a single item or a total purchase amount. For multiple items, sum their prices first and enter the total.

faq.a1: In the US, 15–20% is standard for restaurants, 15% for delivery, and 10–15% for taxis. In many European countries, service is included and a 5–10% tip is optional.
faq.q2: How is the tip calculated?
faq.a2: The tip is a percentage of the bill amount. Multiply the bill by the tip percentage and divide by 100. The total is bill plus tip.
faq.q3: How do I split the bill with tip?
faq.a3: Add the tip to the bill to get the total, then divide the total by the number of people. Each person pays an equal share.
faq.q4: Should I tip on the pre-tax or post-tax amount?
faq.a4: Etiquette varies. Tipping on the pre-tax amount is common and fair, but many people simply tip on the total. Either is generally acceptable.

faq.q1: How do I convert hourly pay to an annual salary?
faq.a1: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For example, $25/hour × 40 hours × 52 weeks = $52,000/year.
faq.q2: How many work hours are there in a year?
faq.a2: A standard full-time schedule (40 hours per week, 52 weeks) is 2,080 hours per year. Part-time and irregular schedules differ.
faq.q3: How do I convert a monthly salary to an hourly rate?
faq.a3: Multiply the monthly salary by 12 to get the annual salary, then divide by the number of working hours per year. For a 40-hour week, that is 2,080 hours.
faq.q4: Does the calculator account for taxes?
faq.a4: No. It converts gross pay only. Taxes and deductions depend on your country, region, and personal situation. Use a separate take-home calculator for net pay.

roi-calculator.title: ROI Calculator – Return on Investment
roi-calculator.description: Free ROI calculator. Compute return on investment, profit and margin for any project or investment.
roi-calculator.keywords: roi calculator,return on investment,investment return,profit margin,roi formula

faq.a1: ROI (Return on Investment) shows how much profit you made relative to the amount invested. Formula: ROI = (final − initial) / initial × 100.
faq.q2: How is ROI different from margin?
faq.a2: ROI compares profit to the amount invested. Margin compares profit to revenue. Both metrics are useful: ROI for investors, margin for businesses.
faq.q3: Can ROI be negative?
faq.a3: Yes. A negative ROI means a loss — the final amount is less than what was invested. ROI of −20% means you lost 20% of your investment.
faq.q4: Does ROI account for time?
faq.a4: Simple ROI does not. A 50% return over one year is very different from 50% over ten years. Use CAGR or annualized return to factor in time.

faq.q1: How is the date difference calculated?
faq.a1: We count the exact number of full years, months and days between the two dates, then convert to totals. This avoids off-by-one errors that appear when using only day counts.
faq.q2: Does the calculator include the end date?
faq.a2: No. The result is the number of days from the start date up to but not including the end date. This matches the standard convention for deadlines and durations.
faq.q3: What if the end date is earlier than the start date?
faq.a3: The calculator automatically swaps them, so you always get a positive result. The order of input does not matter.
faq.q4: How are leap years handled?
faq.a4: Each year is evaluated based on the actual calendar, so February 29 is counted correctly. The month-and-day breakdown respects month lengths automatically.

tdee-macro-calculator.title: TDEE & Macro Calculator – Daily Calories and Macros
tdee-macro-calculator.description: Free TDEE calculator with macro breakdown. Find your Total Daily Energy Expenditure and protein, carb and fat targets for your goal.
tdee-macro-calculator.keywords: tdee calculator,macro calculator,total daily energy expenditure,protein carbs fat,daily calories

faq.a1: TDEE (Total Daily Energy Expenditure) is the total number of calories your body burns per day, including basic functions and physical activity.
faq.q2: How many calories should I eat to lose weight?
faq.a2: A common recommendation is a deficit of 15–20% below TDEE. For a TDEE of 2500 kcal, that is roughly 2000–2100 kcal per day for steady weight loss.
faq.q3: What are good macro ratios for muscle gain?
faq.a3: A common starting point is 25% protein, 45% carbs and 30% fat, with a 15% calorie surplus. Adjust based on your progress over several weeks.
faq.q4: Why is protein important?
faq.a4: Protein supports muscle repair and growth, keeps you full, and preserves lean mass during a cut. 1.6–2.2 g per kg of body weight is a typical range for active adults.

body-fat-calculator.title: Body Fat Calculator – US Navy Method

body-fat-calculator.keywords: body fat calculator,us navy body fat,body fat percentage,lean mass calculator,fat mass

faq.q1: How accurate is the US Navy method?
faq.a1: It is usually accurate within 3–4% of DEXA scans when measurements are taken correctly. Consistency of tape placement matters more than absolute precision.
faq.q2: How do I measure my neck and waist?
faq.a2: Measure the neck just below the larynx, with the tape sloping slightly downward at the front. For waist, measure at the navel for men and at the narrowest point for women.
faq.q3: What is a healthy body fat percentage?
faq.a3: For men, 14–18% is generally considered fit. For women, 21–25%. Essential fat minimums are around 2–5% for men and 10–13% for women.
faq.q4: Does this calculator work for athletes?
faq.a4: It can under- or over-estimate for very muscular or very lean people. For athletes, a DEXA scan or hydrostatic weighing gives more precise results.

ideal-weight-calculator.title: Ideal Weight Calculator – Devine, Robinson, Miller, Hamwi
ideal-weight-calculator.description: Free ideal body weight calculator using four formulas: Devine, Robinson, Miller and Hamwi. Useful for health goals and clinical estimates.
ideal-weight-calculator.keywords: ideal weight calculator,ideal body weight,devine formula,robinson formula,healthy weight

faq.a1: Ideal body weight (IBW) is an estimate of the healthiest weight for your height. It was originally developed for medication dosing but is widely used for general health assessments.
faq.q2: Which formula is most accurate?
faq.a2: None is perfect. Devine is the most common in clinical settings. Robinson, Miller and Hamwi give slightly different results — we average them to smooth out individual formula bias.
faq.q3: Does ideal weight account for muscle mass?
faq.a3: No. These formulas use only height and gender, so they do not distinguish muscle from fat. Muscular people may exceed their IBW while still being healthy.
faq.q4: Is ideal weight the same as a healthy weight range?
faq.a4: No. Ideal weight is a single number. A healthy weight is a range — usually derived from a BMI of 18.5–24.9 for your height. Both are useful as reference points.

water-intake-calculator.title: Water Intake Calculator – Daily Hydration Needs
water-intake-calculator.description: Free water intake calculator. Find out how much water you need daily based on body weight, exercise and climate.
water-intake-calculator.keywords: water intake calculator,daily water needs,hydration calculator,how much water,water per day

faq.q1: How much water should I drink a day?
faq.a1: A common guideline is 30–35 ml per kg of body weight. For a 70 kg adult that is about 2.1–2.5 litres per day from all sources, including food and other drinks.
faq.q2: Does coffee or tea count?
faq.a2: Yes. Despite the mild diuretic effect, coffee and tea still contribute to daily hydration. Most of your fluid intake comes from drinks and about 20% from food.
faq.q3: How much more water do I need when exercising?
faq.a3: Roughly 500 ml for every 30 minutes of moderate exercise. For intense training or hot conditions, this can double — weigh yourself before and after to gauge actual loss.
faq.q4: Can I drink too much water?
faq.a4: Yes. Drinking several litres within a short time can dilute blood sodium (hyponatremia). Spread intake through the day and do not force water beyond thirst during normal activity.

heart-rate-zones-calculator.description: Free heart rate zones calculator. Find your 5 training zones using max heart rate or the Karvonen method. Optimize fat burn, endurance and VO2 max.
heart-rate-zones-calculator.keywords: heart rate zones,max heart rate,karvonen formula,training zones,fat burn zone,cardio zones

faq.q1: How is max heart rate calculated?
faq.a1: The most common formula is 220 − age, which is quick but approximate. More precise methods include the Tanaka formula (208 − 0.7 × age) or a supervised stress test.
faq.q2: What is the Karvonen method?
faq.a2: The Karvonen method uses your heart rate reserve (max HR − resting HR) to set zones. It is more personalized than percentage-of-max because it accounts for your fitness level.
faq.q3: Which zone burns the most fat?
faq.a3: Zone 2 (60–70% of max) burns the highest percentage of fat, but Zone 4 burns more total calories. For weight loss, total energy expenditure matters most.
faq.q4: What is Zone 2 training good for?
faq.a4: Zone 2 builds aerobic base, improves fat oxidation and mitochondrial density. It is the foundation of endurance training and can be done for long durations without excessive fatigue.

pregnancy-due-date-calculator.title: Pregnancy Due Date Calculator – Estimate Your Baby's Arrival
pregnancy-due-date-calculator.description: Free pregnancy due date calculator. Estimate your baby's arrival based on last menstrual period or conception date.
pregnancy-due-date-calculator.keywords: pregnancy due date calculator,due date calculator,pregnancy calculator,estimated due date,pregnancy week

faq.q1: How is the due date calculated?
faq.a1: The standard method (Naegele's rule) adds 280 days (40 weeks) to the first day of your last menstrual period. If you know the conception date, we add 266 days instead.
faq.q2: How accurate is the due date?
faq.a2: Only about 4% of babies are born exactly on the due date. Most arrive within two weeks before or after. An early ultrasound is the most accurate way to estimate.
faq.q3: What are the three trimesters?
faq.a3: First trimester: weeks 1–12. Second: weeks 13–27. Third: weeks 28 to birth. Each trimester has different developmental milestones and screening tests.
faq.q4: Can the due date change?
faq.a4: Yes. If an early ultrasound shows a different gestational age than LMP-based dating, your doctor may adjust the due date — usually only if the difference is more than 5–7 days.

sleep-cycle-calculator.title: Sleep Cycle Calculator – Best Time to Sleep & Wake
sleep-cycle-calculator.description: Free sleep cycle calculator. Find the best times to go to bed or wake up so you finish a full 90-minute cycle and feel more refreshed.
sleep-cycle-calculator.keywords: sleep cycle calculator,sleep calculator,best time to sleep,rem cycle,sleep duration

faq.a1: A sleep cycle is roughly 90 minutes long and includes light sleep, deep sleep and REM. Waking up in the middle of a cycle often feels worse than waking at the end, even after less total sleep.
faq.q2: How many cycles do I need?
faq.a2: Most adults need 5–6 cycles (7.5–9 hours) per night. Athletes and teenagers often need more. Consistently under 4 cycles (6 hours) is linked to health risks.
faq.q3: Why add 15 minutes to bedtime?
faq.a3: Most people take around 15 minutes to fall asleep after getting into bed. The calculator adds this so your cycles line up with actual sleep onset, not lights-out.
faq.q4: Do I need to wake up at the exact cycle end?
faq.a4: No, but aim for it. A variation of 10–15 minutes still feels fine. If you regularly wake groggy, try shifting your bedtime by 15–30 minutes to land better in the cycle.

faq.a1: VO2 max is the maximum rate at which your body can use oxygen during intense exercise. It is the single best indicator of aerobic fitness and cardiovascular health.
faq.q2: How does the Rockport test work?
faq.a2: Walk 1 mile as fast as you can on a flat surface. Immediately record your heart rate and time. The formula estimates VO2 max from age, weight, gender, time and heart rate.
faq.q3: How accurate is the Rockport test?
faq.a3: It correlates within about 10–15% of lab-measured VO2 max. Good for tracking changes over time; less precise for absolute comparison with elite athletes.
faq.q4: What is a good VO2 max?
faq.a4: For men, 45–55 ml/kg/min is good; 55+ is excellent. For women, 40–49 is good; 49+ is excellent. Values decline naturally with age, so age-adjusted norms matter.

faq.q3: Can I pay off sleep debt?
faq.a3: You can recover some of it with extra sleep on weekends, but chronic debt takes consistent good habits over weeks to fully repay. A common approach is to add 1–2 hours of sleep per night until you feel fully rested.
